voyage.name: Santa Maria del Fiore
voyage.content: The cathedral interior is to a basilica pattern; it's vast and at first feels dark and empty. Give your eyes time to adjust, and admire the stained glass windows, funeral monument of Bishop d'Orso, and altar of St Zanobius. Below is the Crypt (M-Sa 10:00-17:00) with remains of the preceding cathedral of Santa Reparata, and the tomb of Brunelleschi. Giotto is believed to lie here somewhere, but his tomb has yet to be

voyage.name: Giotto's Tower
voyage.content: Almost 85 m tall, with 414 steps to climb, this richly decorated tower is topped by an open terrace with a panorama of the Duomo, city and surrounds.

voyage.name: Baptistery
voyage.content: Octagonal plan, with a pyramidal roof covering its dome. It's famous for its bronze doors by Andrea Pisano (14th century) and Lorenzo Ghiberti (15th century) and a beautiful interior vault decorated with 13th-century mosaics. The interior is being restored and is unviewable as of April 2024, though the exterior can be seen.

voyage.name: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo
voyage.alt: Museum of the Works of the Duomo
voyage.content: This houses original artworks from the Duomo and surrounding religious buildings, including sculptures by Donatello, a Michelangelo Pietà (different from his version in Saint Peter's, Rome) and the losing entries in the 1401 contest to design the doors of the Baptistery. Plus models and drawings of the Cathedral.

voyage.name: Galleria degli Uffizi
voyage.price: High season (21 Feb-9 Nov; 21 Dec-9 Jan): adult €29 (or €23 for early morning tickets: 08:15 and 08:30), conc €6, combi with Pitti & Boboli €38; low season: adult €16, conc €6, combi €18; including a booking fee of €4
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 08:15-18:50, Mon closed, last admission 18:00; you may not bring in water
voyage.content: Outstanding fine art museum with Renaissance paintings and sculptures from classical antiquity. It's in a late 16th-century palazzo designed by Vasari, in two wings enclosing a long narrow courtyard, effectively a street, an innovation in its day. Originally the palazzo was magistrates' offices (hence "Uffizi") and state archives; then it came to house the Medici's vast art collection. However, one collections seems

voyage.name: Bargello
voyage.hours: Daily Apr-Oct: 08:15-17:00, Nov-Feb: 08:15-14:00, but closed 2nd & 4th Sun and 1st, 3rd & 5th Mon of each month
voyage.content: Used as a barracks and prison until the 19th century, this museum houses some of the best Renaissance and Mannerist sculpture. Big names here include Michelangelo, Donatello, Ammannati, Bandinelli, Andrea and Jacopo Sansovino, Desiderio da Settignano, Giambologna, and Antonio Rossellino. It also displays ceramics, textiles & tapestries, ivory, silver, armour and coins. Allow two hours. Not nearly as crowded as the Uf

voyage.name: Galleria dell'Accademia
voyage.content: Highlights are Michelangelo's original David (the one in Piazza della Signoria is a copy) and his unfinished Slaves. It also includes Florentine painting, a museum of musical instruments, and Russian icons. No photography is allowed inside. N.B. the "Accademia di Belle Arti" next door is a university department, not connected with the Gallery.

voyage.name: Palazzo Pitti
voyage.price: Mar-Oct: adult €16, conc €8, combi with Uffizi & Boboli €38; Nov-Feb: adult €10, conc €5, combi €18; booking fee €4
voyage.content: The original Pitti was a banker; the palace has housed royalty but became best known for its Medici family treasures. It's now divided into four museums (same ticket): ground floor is the Treasury of the Grand Dukes; first floor houses the Palatine Gallery and the Royal and Imperial Apartments, second floor is the Modern Art Gallery and the Museum of Costume and Fashion. The Boboli gardens are just behind the palazzo

voyage.name: Palazzo Davanzati
voyage.content: a house museum with antique fittings and furniture

voyage.name: Museo Galileo
voyage.content: This museum shows the evolution of the instruments used in various scientific fields such as mathematics, physics, biology, chemistry, astronomy. The room of Galileo Galilei shows some of his original instruments as well as models from his drawings. The room of Spheres and Globes houses an excellent cartographic collection. In a rather macabre twist the museum also has the middle finger of Galileo's right hand on dis

voyage.name: Museo Horne
voyage.address: Palazzo Corsi on via dei Benci, 6
voyage.content: Displays art and furnishings of the 14th & 15th century. The building and art collection were owned by art historian Herbert Percy Horne.

voyage.name: Archaeological Museum
voyage.content: The Etruscan art collection is particularly good.

voyage.name: Museo Novecento
voyage.hours: Sat-Wed 11:00-20:00, Thu 11:00-14:00, Fri 11:00-23:00, Firenze Cardholder free
voyage.content: Gallery of 20th- & 21st-century art, on three floors of a palazzo.

voyage.name: Museo Marini
voyage.content: Houses the work of that contemporary sculptor.

voyage.name: Stibbert Museum
voyage.content: Has a great collection of armour and arms.

voyage.name: Palazzo Vecchio
voyage.price: "Museum" or "Tower and Battlements": €12.50 adults, €10 concessions. "Museum" and "Tower and Battlements": €17.50 adults, €15 concessions
voyage.content: Old city palace/city hall, adorned with fine art. The replica of Michelangelo's "David" is placed outside the main door in the original location of the statue, which is a symbol of the Comune of Florence. The site displays an important collection of Renaissance sculptures and paintings, including the Putto by Verrochio and the series of murals by Giorgio Vasari at the Salone dei Cinquecento (Hall of the Five Hundreds

voyage.name: Ponte Vecchio
voyage.content: The oldest and most celebrated bridge over the Arno, and the only Florentine bridge to survive World War II. The design is distinctive: it's a three-arched bridge supporting a parade of shops supporting another bridge. It dates to 1345 (hence Ponte Vecchio, "old bridge"), with earlier bridges being swept away by floods, rebuilt and swept away again. At street level it's a pedestrianised cobbled arch. It's lined by sh

voyage.name: Santa Croce
voyage.content: Contains the monumental tombs of Galileo, Michelangelo, Machiavelli, Dante, Rossini, and many other notables in addition to artistic decorations. There is also great artwork in the church. The Museo dell'Opera di Santa Croce (included in ticket) displays a flood-damaged but still beautiful Crucifix by Cimabue (Giotto's teacher), which has become a symbol of the disastrous floods of 1966. The ticket also includes Pazz

voyage.name: Santa Maria Novella
voyage.content: A beautiful church with great artwork, including a Trinity by Masaccio that is being restored as of April 2024 but can still be seen from the scaffold for an additional charge of €1.50 and a great series of frescoes by Ghirlandaio behind the altar. Also, the museum near the Chiostro Verde, outside the church to its left (follow the signs in the church), contains gently restored frescoes of Old Testament scenes by Pao

voyage.name: Orsanmichele
voyage.content: A beautiful old church from the 14th century, which once functioned as a grain market.

voyage.name: San Lorenzo
voyage.content: The façade of this church was never completed, giving it a striking, rustic appearance. Inside the church is pure Renaissance neo-classical splendor. If you go around the back of the church, there is a separate entrance to the Medici chapels. Be sure to check out the stunning burial chapel of the princes and the sacristy down the corridor. The small sacristy is blessed with the presence of nine Michelangelo sculpture

voyage.name: San Marco Convent
voyage.content: Houses frescoes by Fra Angelico and his workshop. Fra Angelico painted a series of frescoes for the cells in which the Dominican monks lived.

voyage.name: Great Synagogue and Jewish Museum of Florence
voyage.price: €6.50 total for the synagogue and museum
voyage.hours: Jun-Sep: Mon-Thu 10:00 - 18:30, Fri 10:00 - 17:00; Oct-May: Sun-Thu 10:00 - 17:30, Fri 10:00 - 15:00. Closed except for religious services on Saturdays and Jewish holidays
voyage.content: Lovely Moorish-style synagogue built in 1882 and a museum with many artefacts and documentation of Florentine Jewish life going back many centuries; audio tours in multiple languages are available.

voyage.name: The English Cemetery
voyage.content: In the 19th century, the "English Cemetery" received anyone that the city's churchyards wouldn't receive, e.g. Orthodox Christians, but Britons and Americans were the majority. Famous names here include Elizabeth Barrett Browning, Fanny Trollope and Beatrice Shakespeare, a relative of William. There are lots of ornate gravestones with flowery inscriptions in multiple languages.

voyage.name: Piazza della Signoria
voyage.content: Piazza della Signoria is the grand open space in front: not quite a square, as Palazzo Vecchio blocks out one corner. Sights here are the equestrian statue of Cosimo de Medici, the Fountain of Neptune, the statue of David, and Loggia dei Lanzi, an open arched gallery of Renaissance sculpture

voyage.name: Santa Felicita
voyage.content: Contains frescoes of the Annunciation and a painting of the Deposition of Christ by the brilliant and weird mannerist painter, Pontormo. They are to be found in the Barbadori Chapel, which is to your immediate right when entering the church.

voyage.name: Boboli Gardens
voyage.content: Elaborately landscaped and with many interesting sculptures, behind the Pitti Palace. Wonderful city views. Don't miss the Bardini gardens. Entrance to that is included in the combination ticket price for the Boboli, and it's a short walk from the Boboli Gardens. There are great views of the Duomo from the Bardini gardens.

voyage.name: Santa Maria del Carmine
voyage.content: Famous frescoes (Masaccio’s Adam and Eve Banished From the Garden and others by Lippi and Masolino) in the Brancacci Chapel.

voyage.name: Piazzale Michelangelo
voyage.content: Plaza on a hillside with a great view of the city. Go there by bus or climb the stairs and paths from the Lungarno della Zecca.

voyage.name: San Miniato al Monte
voyage.content: The Sacristy contains frescoes by Spinello Aretino. In the cemetery near this church there are graves of famous people of Florence, including Carlo Lorenzi (Collodi) - author of the famous Pinocchio. Also, turn around when you reach the top of the stairs before entering the church, to see perhaps an even greater view of the city than from nearby Piazzale Michelangelo.

voyage.name: Enjoy the view from the Piazzale Michelangelo
voyage.content: It's a big square on a hill, but somewhat distant from the traditional tourist sites. It's easy to reach it even on foot using the stairs called "Rampe di San Niccolò". They are on the side of the Arno RIver just in front of the national library. Do this during the summer and during the night to admire Florence's lights.

voyage.name: Firenze Rafting
voyage.address: Arno riverbank in front of the Torre San Niccolò
voyage.content: Guided rafting trips on the Arno through the historic centre, passing beneath Ponte Vecchio. Tours last about one hour, require no previous experience and are run in inflatable rafts with an instructor in each boat. Equipment is provided; participants should expect to get wet. Booking in advance is required.

voyage.name: Impruneta spa
voyage.content: The thermal waters of Impruneta spring from two sources and are used to treat respiratory diseases, liver, gastrointestinal, and skin allergies.

voyage.name: Florence Photography Workshop & Tour
voyage.content: Discover Florence with your camera and with a professional photography teacher (a Vogue-featured American photographer) and an official Florence guide at your side.

voyage.name: ABC School
voyage.content: Italian language school offering language and cultural courses since 1982.

voyage.name: Centro Machiavelli
voyage.content: Italian language and cultural school for foreigners. The structure and the contents of the programmes for the levels are based on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. The school also organises a programme of cultural activities and excursions to complement the language classes and enable the students to come into contact with the Italian culture and practice Italian in the field.

voyage.name: Istituto Galilei
voyage.content: Italian language school specializing in one-to-one, personalized and small group (max 4 people) full immersion courses.

voyage.name: Michelangelo Institute
voyage.content: Italian study programmes for foreign students. Cooking workshop, art history classes, plastic arts and visual arts programs are also taught in this academy.

voyage.name: Scuola Leonardo da Vinci Florence
voyage.content: Offers a wide choice of Italian language and culture courses for children and adults from beginning to advanced levels.

voyage.name: Cooking Class
voyage.content: Florence and Tuscany are becoming synonymous with "cooking class". Tuscan cuisine is appreciated worldwide and a cooking class experience is now more and more part of the attraction of Tuscany, as a way of carrying back home memories and improved cooking skills. There are many in the area, either in historical villas in the countryside or in central Florence, from Florentine use of tripe and giblets to the use of org

voyage.name: Enoteca Mondovino
voyage.content: Decent wine and liquor store with interesting collection of potable bitters in the back (Italian and German).

voyage.name: Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella
voyage.content: With roots dating to 1221, this shop sells high-quality beauty products like soaps, shaving cream, eau de Cologne and Carta D'Armenia incense papers in a shop that was once the chapel of San Niccolò.Worth entering even just to see the space and smell the herbal products made from historic recipes. Has a nice cafe on site, with plenty of herbal teas.

voyage.name: Pitti Vintage - Italian & European Vintage Clothing & Accessories
voyage.content: Fendi, Ferragamo, Gucci, Lancetti, Valentino. Specializes in Italian and European designer and one-of-a-kind vintage pieces.

voyage.name: Cose Del 900 - Italian Glass Connection
voyage.content: Since 1981 specializing in sized-to-order, affordable beaded jewelry featuring handmade Murano glass beads.

voyage.name: Ortigia SRL
voyage.content: Luxurious soaps, scents, creams, candles and lotions inspired by the aesthetics, colours, and scents of Sicily.

voyage.name: Albrici
voyage.content: Long-established antiques and home decor store located among the traditional artisans' workshops of Oltrarno. Within it, Recollection sells vintage clothing and accessories.

voyage.name: I fratellini
voyage.content: Good street food: panini for €5 (Mar 2024) and wine for €2+ (Oct 2018) from a tiny hole in the wall. Patrons eat on the sidewalk while resting their glass of wine on small shelves nested along the street wall.

voyage.name: Trattoria Mario
voyage.content: Lunch only, no booking, you'll be seated with other walk-ins. Good food, try to save room for a meat main course.

voyage.name: Trattoria Le Mossacce
voyage.content: Reliable local eatery. Local produce and meats are prepared simply using traditional recipes and time-honoured tradition. Some pastas are made fresh daily, so ask for the daily special. If you want to experience Bistecca alla Fiorentina (Florentine-style steak), they do it amazingly without breaking your wallet. They sell and cut the steak from a larger rib slab in increments of 100g (with a minimum of 500g per servi

voyage.name: Self-Service Ristorante Leonardo
voyage.price: Primi €3.5-4. Secondi €4.5-5.5. About €10 per person for a full-course dinner (Oct 2018)
voyage.content: Although there is a menu at the entrance, it is better to go straight in and pick what you like. You can also order Bistecca alla Fiorentina.

voyage.name: Tiona Asian Restaurant
voyage.content: Not that you'd admit to wanting a break from Italian food, but this small friendly Sri Lankan restaurant makes a refreshing change. Ayubowan!

voyage.name: Pescheria Sugarello
voyage.content: Seafood. Excellent fried calamari and grilled fish fillet with vegetables. You can find also fresh oysters. Be there early, as it gets packed very easily.

voyage.name: Amici di Ponte Vecchio
voyage.content: Pizza, schiacciata, homemade sandwiches, wine by the glass, takeaway.

voyage.name: Il Vegetariano
voyage.content: Budget restaurant with more formal front room, the eclectic middle room, or the peaceful outdoor garden in the back. Daily changing menu with vegan and gluten-free items clearly marked, desserts, salads, soups, hearty brown bread, and a good selection of coffee, tea, wine, beer, and liqueur.

voyage.name: Trattoria Zà Zà
voyage.content: A very nicely decorated restaurant with many vegetarian choices. You can choose to sit inside or outside in the piazza. The menu is huge, lots of choices, and the prices are fair. Service is outstanding, they really cater to your needs. Make sure to try the chianti house wine. Note that they have two seating areas on the piazza: between are two other restaurants, Cantastorie and Garibaldi.

voyage.name: al Tranvai
voyage.content: Tourists seldom venture this far south. Traditional Tuscan food at decent prices. 1st courses at €7, mains at €10 to €16 and vino at €4 / 0.5L (Oct 2018). The rabbit, asparagus souffle and fiori fritti are excellent and the service very welcoming and warm.

voyage.name: "Il Latini" Restaurant
voyage.content: Fun place, communal seating and lively staff. The steaks are good.

voyage.name: Trattoria Palle D'Oro dal 1860
voyage.content: Long-standing family-run Tuscan restaurant. This is where the locals come, not least for the low prices. Fixed price 2-course lunch or €13, dinner €14 (Oct 2018)

voyage.name: Trattoria Cammillo
voyage.content: Fairly good Tuscan cuisine, with a number of options for vegetarians and vegans. Make reservations or be there as they open.

voyage.name: Enoteca Pinchiorri
voyage.content: Michelin-starred restaurant with exquisite meals at splurge prices.

voyage.name: B-Roof
voyage.content: Fine dining with wonderful night panorama of the city.

voyage.name: Il Cibreo
voyage.content: Great choice of Tuscan food, with highly selected ingredients.

voyage.name: Trattoria da Tito
voyage.content: Although a bit of a walk from the main attractions, this restaurant speaks for itself with mandatory reservations. Great Italian food and atmosphere. Dinner often includes impromptu free drinks and lively table staff.

voyage.name: Gelateria dei Neri
voyage.content: Ice cream in many flavors, some experimental, all excellent.

voyage.name: Festival Del Gelato
voyage.content: 50 flavors and has an upbeat atmosphere

voyage.name: Vivoli
voyage.content: Via Isole delle Stinche, 7/R. Close to Piazza Santa Croce. Vivoli has a good gelato fruit selection, so definitely try the fragola, or strawberry. Make sure that you ask for the cream on top as well, because it adds another element to an already great dessert.

voyage.name: La Cite
voyage.content: A very nice and cozy cafe/bookstore. Good prices, nice atmosphere, good books. Borgo San Frediano 20r.

voyage.name: Enoteca Le volpi e l'Uva
voyage.content: The must of the tasting wines and savory titbits. Piazza dei Rossi, 1.

voyage.name: Été
voyage.content: A lovely little café with warm service and good local beer and wine.

voyage.name: Cavalli Club
voyage.content: Roberto Cavalli, Italian fashion designer, has one his beautiful clubs in Florence. The inside has a stage with a projector of Roberto Cavalli's fashion shows running non-stop. The upstairs can be a private lounge for parties or VIP section on certain nights. This club was the most popular on Wednesday nights, but it’s open on the weekends as well. It’s black and leopard interior fits the natural and animalistic desi

voyage.name: Bamboo Lounge Club
voyage.content: Bamboo Lounge Club is a great place for young adults and students to party. The music is great from European to American techno and many other worldwide DJs. Bamboo Lounge Club offers VIP tables and has two midsized bars. It is very clean and safe to be in. It is located on Via Giuseppe Verdi not far from the Duomo. Dress is a little more than casual, but not too upscale. The loud music, dancing, and exciting atmosph

voyage.name: Tenax
voyage.content: If you love house and electronic music this is the best club to go to. It’s a two-story club, located on the outskirts of Florence, features DJ’s from all around Europe, America, and Australia. This club also holds many concerts during the winter and summer. Many people come from all over to enjoy this club's atmosphere. The dance floor is extremely large and is always very crowded. Be smart where you keep your bag a

voyage.name: Hostel Florence Experience
voyage.content: A hostel in a historic Florentine noble palace built in the 14th century and modified in the 17th century. Rooms are occasionally clean.

voyage.name: Hostel Archi Rossi
voyage.content: Never mind the renaissance-kitsch walls. Rooms are clean and rates include breakfast, dinner (except Saturdays) and internet access.

voyage.name: Hostel 7 Santi
voyage.content: A converted 19th-century convent. Rooms are clean and quiet. Has dorm bunks and private rooms.

voyage.name: B&B Duomo View
voyage.content: Large choice of double bedrooms. Services are in common and some of the guestrooms boast a fantastic view of the Duomo. Internet connection and breakfast also available.

voyage.name: B&B Giglio Bianco
voyage.content: This B&B has just the one room, the Camera Verde. They feature gourmet meals and cooking classes directed by Chef Vary.

voyage.name: B&B di Piazza del Duomo
voyage.content: A small B&B, rooms with private bathroom and shower, A/C, LCD TV, free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: B&B Tourist House Battistero
voyage.content: A lovely B&B in the centre, with the Duomo just 30 m away.

voyage.name: Florence Stadium B&B
voyage.content: 3-star with clean, spacious rooms near the Stadium and Mandela Forum.

voyage.name: Giulia Residence
voyage.content: Decent 3-star, access through clanky iron gate in apartment block.

voyage.name: Opera Boutique B&B
voyage.content: Historic building of the late nineteenth century.

voyage.name: Arizona Hotel
voyage.content: This 3-star hotel is in a renovated villa from the 18th century.

voyage.name: Convitto della Calza
voyage.content: 3 star in converted 16th-century cloister, with frescoed rooms and a modern conference centre.

voyage.name: Hotel Desirèe
voyage.content: Friendly 3-star with 18 rooms, next to railway station.

voyage.name: Hotel Byron
voyage.content: Three-star hotel with parking.

voyage.name: Hotel Casci
voyage.content: This small 2-star is in a 15th-century palace and has some original fresco ceilings. Composer Gioacchino Rossini lived here in the 19th century.

voyage.name: Hotel Dali
voyage.content: One star, consistently clean & cosy, good location, owners Marco and Samanta helpful and fluent in English.

voyage.name: Hotel Fiorita
voyage.content: Next to railway station, on 3rd floor of building that has two other hotels. Rooms have a/c, TV and a safety deposit box. Some rooms also have modem sockets.

voyage.name: Hotel Masaccio
voyage.content: Cozy one-star in a 20th-century villa, with restaurant.

voyage.name: Hotel Giglio
voyage.content: Simple 3-star on edge of centro storico.

voyage.name: Hotel Kursaal & Ausonia
voyage.content: A small 2-star, basic but clean.

voyage.name: Hotel Lorena
voyage.content: Two-star hotel in the historic centre, simple but comfy.

voyage.name: Hotel Montreal
voyage.content: Two star, central but basic and dated.

voyage.name: Hotel Palazzuolo
voyage.content: Basic 2-star, many stairs & no lift, but central.

voyage.name: Hotel Romagna
voyage.content: Two-star hotel near SMN train station. 22 bedrooms en suite, internet connection and satellite TV. Cosy (ie small rooms, basic), no lift to upper floors.

voyage.name: Hotel Delle Tele
voyage.content: Central 3-star near SMN Duomo.

voyage.name: Albergo Firenze
voyage.content: 2-star hotel, central but basic.

voyage.name: Il Bargello B&B
voyage.content: Clean friendly 3-star.

voyage.name: FH Calzaiuoli Hotel
voyage.content: Central 4-star going on 3.

voyage.name: Hotel Caravaggio
voyage.content: Good 3-star, consistently clean, well-run & helpful.

voyage.name: Galileo Hotel
voyage.content: 3 star in an elegant 19th-century building, but a/c and wifi erratic.

voyage.name: Hotel Basilea Florence
voyage.content: This 3-star hotel offers 38 bedrooms, single, double, twin, triple and 2 large suites, all with private bath, television and internet connection.

voyage.name: Hotel Boston
voyage.content: 3-star hotel with 16 bedrooms, not all en-suite. Clean but small and basic.

voyage.name: Hotel Crocini
voyage.content: Central 2-star, not all rooms en suite.

voyage.name: Hotel La Gioconda
voyage.content: 3-star hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Il Guelfo Bianco
voyage.content: 3-star in a 15th-century building.

voyage.name: Hotel Malaspina
voyage.content: 3-star in charming a late 19th-century residence, enriched with modern comforts.

voyage.name: Hotel Marignolle
voyage.address: Via di San Quirichino a Marignolle 16
voyage.content: 4-star in hills outside town, in bosky Tuscan scenery. Outdoor pool May to October.

voyage.name: Hotel Mario's
voyage.content: Central 3-star.

voyage.name: Hotel Mia Cara
voyage.content: Small 3-star a short walk from Santa Maria Novella. Friendly English-speaking staff.

voyage.name: Hotel Morandi alla Crocetta
voyage.content: Comfy 3-star in a Dominican 16th-century convent. On-site garage parking is available.

voyage.name: Privilege Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star hotel on the bank of the Arno, with single, double, triple and "Family" rooms. Breakfast buffet, hotel bar and garage available.

voyage.name: Relais Villa Antea
voyage.content: Historical residence in an old palazzo with friendly staff. Rooms are spacious.

voyage.name: Hotel Rivoli
voyage.content: 4-star in a former 14th-century Franciscan convent.

voyage.name: Hotel De Rose Palace
voyage.content: 4-star hotel in a traditional Florentine mansion.

voyage.name: Hotel Savonarola
voyage.content: 3-star with one single and 15 twin, double, triple and quadruple rooms. All with private bath, Wi-Fi connection, telephone and breakfast included.

voyage.name: Novotel Firenze Nord Aeroporto
voyage.content: 4-star handy for airport. Well out of city but they have free shuttle to the city center.

voyage.name: Villa il Mosaico
voyage.content: Elegant villa, ten self-catering apartments with kitchen, living room, bathroom, internet connection and TV. Private parking and 100 square metre terrace with solarium.

voyage.name: Residence Select Executive
voyage.content: 4-star hotel; 12 rooms, some with kitchenette.

voyage.name: Hotel Unicorno
voyage.content: Small 3-star hotel in a 17th-century building.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Adriatico
voyage.content: Modern 4-star hotel in the historical centre, very close to the train station. Rooms and suites are suitable for couples, families, single travellers and group of friends. The hotel features a Tuscan restaurant, a private car park, complimentary breakfast served on a terrace on the ground floor and free minibar for direct bookings.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Cavour
voyage.content: Friendly, efficient hotel in a 13th-century palazzo. Former residence of the Strozzi-Ridolfi dynasty.

voyage.name: J and J Hotel
voyage.content: 4-star hotel in former convent. Has double, twin, junior suite, suite, and double rooms for single use, all en-suite services.

voyage.name: Kraft Hotel
voyage.content: 4-star hotel near the centre with swimming-pool, restaurant and 5th-floor terrace with bar.

voyage.name: Hotel Laurus al Duomo
voyage.content: A historic 4-star hotel, close to the Cathedral and Firenze SMN railway station.

voyage.name: Milu Hotel
voyage.content: Central 4-star with roof garden with a charming view.

voyage.name: Hotel Mirage
voyage.price: Single from €110, doubles from €140, triples from €160, apartments from €300 per week
voyage.content: Comfortable straightforward 4-star hotel with restaurant. Regard this as an airport hotel and you won't be disappointed.

voyage.name: Hotel Monna Lisa Florence
voyage.content: Four-star hotel, and yes it's Monna, that's not a typo. In a restored 14th-century Florentine noble palace. Gym facilities, sun terrace and meeting rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel Ponte Vecchio Suites & Spa
voyage.content: 4-star hotel with modern rooms and suites. The hotel offers a private spa for two with a hot tub. Continental breakfast and free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: NH Porta Rossa
voyage.content: Gorgeous hotel built in the 12th century.

voyage.name: L'Orologia
voyage.content: Swanky boutique 4-star hotel with rooms themed on watches. Nice view of Piazza & Basilica from breakfast room.

voyage.name: Orto de' Medici
voyage.content: 4-star hotel in a 19th-century building with gardens.

voyage.name: Palazzo Magnani Feroni
voyage.content: It's in a 16th-century building that belonged to Marquis Feroni. It has twelve comfortable suites with classic furniture and original frescoes.

voyage.name: Residence La Repubblica Florence
voyage.content: 21 self-catering apartments for a maximum of six people, all with kitchenette, private bath, internet connection, satellite TV and cooking facilities. Short stays (eg single night) welcome.

voyage.name: Hotel Pitti Palace al Ponte Vecchio
voyage.content: 4-star overlooking the bridge; you're paying for the location.

voyage.name: Villa Poggio ai Merli
voyage.content: A historic residence on edge of city, in large park.

voyage.name: Villa la Vedetta
voyage.content: 5-star luxury hotel with panorama of Florence's skyline.

voyage.name: Hotel degli Orafi
voyage.content: Boutique 4-star in Florence city centre, overlooking river near Ponte Vecchio.

voyage.name: Palazzo Vecchietti
voyage.content: Historic residence a few steps from Piazza della Repubblica, in the centre of Florence. Few suites, elegant and modern. The hotel also offers two apartments in the central area. Gluten-free products and breakfast included in the room rate.

voyage.name: DoubleTree by Hilton Florence Metropole
voyage.price: from €80 for a King Guest Room to €150 for a suite
voyage.content: A 4-star hotel with views of the city. A spa, fitness centre, room service and business centre are available on site.

voyage.name: Ad Astra Florence
voyage.content: A historic residence with 14 rooms enriched by frescoed ceilings and individually furnished with elegant vintage, classic and contemporary touches. The most prestigious rooms and the living room are surrounded by a terrace overlooking the Torrigiani Garden.

voyage.name: Palazzo Firenze by Baglioni Hotels & Resorts
voyage.content: 5-star hotel in Florence’s historic Santa Croce district, set in an elegant 18th-century palazzo. Offers classic Florentine-style rooms with high ceilings, marble bathrooms, and parquet floors. Refined and quiet, with gourmet dining and easy access to major landmarks (meals not included).
